name: Lugaid mac Lóegairi
summary:
Lugaid mac Lóegairi was a High King of Ireland from 436 to 507 CE, succeeding his father Niall of the Nine Hostages and grandson of Niall. His reign saw significant conflict with neighboring kingdoms, including the Ulaid and Connachta, leading to several major battles.

Lugaid's strategic alliances with other Celtic leaders helped maintain Irish independence during a tumultuous period of European history. However, his aggressive expansion into neighboring territories ultimately led to the decline of the High King's authority.

Despite this, Lugaid mac Lóegairi left an enduring legacy in Irish mythology and historical record, solidifying his place as one of Ireland's most influential monarchs.

"The lands of Éirinn will not be conquered by the forces of Ulster." Lugaid mac Lóegairi famously declared during a battle against his enemies, cementing his reputation as a fierce defender of Irish sovereignty.
